content.name: Iván Manfredi
content.basis_note:
This is built from the 30 posts you published in the last year, which is where your voice is easiest to see, plus the long-form writing on your profile.

Every line quoted back to you is yours, copied as you wrote it.
summary: You write in short declarative bursts: 447 sentences across 30 posts, median 9 words, with 40% of them running under 8 words. Someone landing cold gets the rhythm of a person talking across a table, plain and direct sentence after sentence.

You address one reader and you address them directly. Your pronoun counts sit almost level, I at 2.6 per 100 words and you at 2.5, so the reader is always in the room while you are the one carrying the story.

Proof arrives as digits: 25 of the 30 pieces carry a number, 12 carry a percentage, and those numbers usually sit in a bare line by themselves. The reader walks away holding one figure and one decision attached to it.
The exits are quiet. 10 of your 30 posts end on a line of 8 words or fewer, and 0 of them ask anyone to like, comment or repost, so the last line is an instruction or a verdict, never a request.

traits.name: You drop numbers on their own line
traits.what_you_do: When a figure carries the argument, you break the paragraph and let the number stand alone with nothing around it. 12 of your 30 pieces carry a percentage, and 57% of your 268 paragraphs are a single sentence, so the number gets its own white space.
traits.use_it: Take the strongest figure in your next post, cut it out of the sentence it lives in, and give it a paragraph of its own.
traits.quote:
Warm invites: 32.8% accepted. 21 of 64.

Cold: 7.5%. 4 of 53.

traits.name: You start the story with a stranger
traits.what_you_do: Your case posts open on a person you talked to, described by role, before any claim appears. The I shows up after the setup, which is why only 2 of your 30 posts open on I or my.
traits.use_it: Open your next case post by naming the role and the one number that defines their situation. Hold your own view until the third paragraph.
traits.quote: I talked to a marketing agency co-founder last week whose biggest client is close to 40% of her revenue.

traits.name: You close on a short command
traits.what_you_do: Your last line is often a verb pointed at the reader, 8 words or fewer, with no ask attached. 10 of your 30 posts end this short, and 0 end on a request to comment, repost or DM.
traits.use_it: End your next post with one imperative under 8 words that names the exact action, then stop typing.
traits.quote: Every post from me clears that same gate. Build stage two.

traits.name: You start sentences on But and So
traits.what_you_do: You hinge a paragraph by opening it with a conjunction, which turns the break into the pivot. 35 of your 447 sentences start on And, But, So or Because, and 30 of your 268 paragraph openings do the same.
traits.use_it: Find the turn in your next post, break the paragraph there, and open the new one with But or So.
traits.quote: But the audience is too cold and small in month one to produce pipeline on its own.

traits.name: You write the arrow, never the emoji
traits.what_you_do: Your lists run on arrows and digits and hyphens: → 20 times, 1. 18 times, - 18 times. Across 30 posts you used 0 emoji in the running text and 1 exclamation mark, so the visual marks do the work punctuation would.
traits.use_it: In your next list, use → for parallel items and 1. for ordered steps. Add no emoji and no bold.
traits.quote:
→ Create demand around a problem your ICP already has

→ Give you a point of view people can remember

traits.name: You quote the client raw
traits.what_you_do: When the proof is something a person said, you reproduce the line in their wording, hesitations and filler left in. You place it next to the role, so the reader can see the source of the claim.
traits.use_it: Pull one sentence from a call transcript into your next post word for word. Fix nothing in it.
traits.quote: "I don't want to be the bottleneck, and the amount of information that I know stops us from growing past what I know."

traits.name: You let the swearing through
traits.what_you_do: Your register drops to spoken register when the point is blunt, with contractions running all the way through: 101 of them across 25 of the 30 pieces. The informal line sits right next to the percentages without changing gear.
traits.use_it: Read your next draft aloud. Where you would say it looser in conversation, write the looser version down.
traits.quote: Two moves: Posting and DMs. That's it lol

signature_moves.move: You set up a list by stating the thing the list will fix, then breaking to a colon or a bare line before the marks start. The reader gets the frame in one line, then the items land with nothing explaining them.
You ask a question in the middle of a piece and answer it in the next line, in one or two beats. The question sits alone as its own paragraph, so the hinge is visible before the answer arrives.
signature_moves.quote:
So? 

He will book more calls and make more money.

signature_moves.move: Your proof arrives as two bare numbers on consecutive lines with the labels stripped down, and only after them do you say what the comparison means. The arithmetic goes in its own sentence below.
signature_moves.quote:
Warm invites: 32.8% accepted. 21 of 64.

Cold: 7.5%. 4 of 53.

signature_moves.move: Your last line is often an instruction stripped to the verb, landing after a paragraph that did the reasoning. No sign-off sits under it.
signature_moves.quote: Every post from me clears that same gate. Build stage two.

signature_moves.move: In the middle of a case piece you concede the objection in one short paragraph, then keep going in the next one. The concession gets its own break so the reader sees you handle it before the point resumes.
signature_moves.quote: A folder of transcripts does nothing on its own though. The folder was the part that was broken.

content.ghostwriter_brief:
Write as Iván talking to one person he already knows: an agency owner or founder, across a table. The register is spoken, with contractions running through it, 101 of them across 25 of his 30 pieces.

Sentences stay short. 447 of them, median 9 words, 40% under 8 words and only 3% over 25.

Paragraphs are 268 across 30 posts, median 14 words, 8.9 a piece, and 57% of them are a single sentence. 30 of those paragraph openings start on And, But, So or Because, which is how a break becomes a pivot.

Open on a statement or a figure. 6 of the 30 posts put a number inside the first 8 words, 2 open on I or my, 4 open on you or your, 0 open on a question and 0 open on a time marker such as last week.

Land quiet. 10 of the 30 posts end on a line of 8 words or fewer, often a verb pointed at the reader, and 0 end on an ask to comment, repost or DM.

Proof comes as digits. 25 of the 30 pieces carry a number, 12 carry a percentage, 4 carry a money figure, and the figure gets its own line with nothing around it before the sentence that says what it means.

Quote the client in their own wording, hesitations left in, sitting next to their role.

Keep these words: agency owner, sales calls, lead magnet, qualifying question, calls a month, kept extending, the exact buyer he sells to, actually, already, founders, ICP.

Keep out the decorative punctuation: across 4610 words there are 0 long dashes, 0 semicolons, 2 ellipses, 1 exclamation mark. 0 emoji. Lists run on → 20 times, 1. 18 times, - 18 times. Of 26 corporate filler words checked, 1 occurrence total.

The giveaway is a closing line that asks for something.
